text:
I will say it at the start

for whoever wants to understand:

they are sorrows piled high,

to be poor and be a woman.


She works her whole life

barely enough to eat.

She has the sorrows of the poor

and, on top of that, those of being a woman.


The rich woman has rights,

the poor woman has duties.

It is already much to suffer for being poor

and on top of that for being a woman.


She is so helpless

and is mother and father at once.

Rights, not even the right to complain,

for being poor and being a woman.


Many speeches are made

about her heroism of yesterday.

On paper they respect her.

But only on paper.


And I repeat it again

for whoever wants to understand:

they are sorrows piled high,

to be poor and be a woman.

translation.title: Stacked Sorrows
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated, songlike indictment of class and gender oppression.
